payload.report: CTA directly reveals a 20 mm pseudoaneurysm at the distal aortic graft anastomosis and a residual false lumen in the brachiocephalic artery, directly refuting the stable postoperative hypothesis and strongly supporting aortic graft/vascular dysfunction. The patent coronary graft does not mitigate these serious findings. ECG evidence supports first-degree AV block and echocardiography supports LV diastolic dysfunction, but these are secondary. Lack of prior imaging comparison leaves uncertainty about progression speed, yet the imaging and radiologist interpretation confirm the diagnosis of aortic graft pseudoaneurysm with residual false lumen, requiring urgent vascular surgical evaluation.
